items.text: Exhaustive action inventory is now complete: deployment-manager (86+ API endpoints, 50+ CLI commands, 8 UI pages), scenario-to-desktop (60+ API endpoints, 40+ CLI commands, 5 UI tabs), LPBS (15 download-related API endpoints, 16 CLI commands, 4 database tables), scenario-to-cloud (70+ API endpoints, 50+ CLI commands), and 3 prompt-manager skills encoding the full pipeline workflow.

Code-only validation confirmed the data flow diagram. scenario-to-desktop's deploy stage calls LPBS via lpbs_client.go (presign→upload→commit→apply). deployment-manager's desktop_client.go calls scenario-to-desktop's pipeline/run endpoint. scenario-to-cloud's freshness.go compares deployed service.json version with local version. All routes verified against route registration files.

Auth boundary discovery: LPBS presign-upload and commit accept admin OR service auth (requireAdminOrService middleware), but set-current is admin-only (requireAdmin). scenario-to-desktop's deploy stage uses service auth, so it goes through apply (which accepts service auth) rather than set-current. This is a subtle but important distinction for the system contract.

System contracts for all 5 systems have been drafted as interface boundary documents (per round 1 decision d2=A). Each contract defines: what the system owns (source of truth), what it exposes (APIs others depend on), what it consumes (APIs it calls), and what it assumes (implicit contracts).

items.context: The plan is now substantially complete: all 5 audit questions are answered with evidence, the action inventory is exhaustive, system contracts are drafted, gaps are cataloged, and prioritized recommendations are included. The remaining items from the Definition of Done are peer review passes. The question is whether to close this research item or run one more round.

options.label: Close after this round — mark ready for review
options.rationale: All Definition of Done checkboxes are met except peer review, which happens outside this workshop. The plan is comprehensive enough for downstream implementation items to reference. Marking ready lets the review happen asynchronously.

options.label: Run one more round for edge cases
options.rationale: Could add: detailed request/response schemas for each inter-system call, sequence diagrams in mermaid format, or validation against a real running instance. Adds polish but delays availability.

items.topic: Should gap recommendations become individual backlog items now?
items.context: The plan includes 7 prioritized gap recommendations (P1-P4). These could be converted into individual backlog items immediately (as part of this research item's output), or left as recommendations in the document for a human or the initiative owner to triage later.

options.label: Create backlog items now for P1 and P2 gaps
options.rationale: The 4 highest-priority gaps (git commit traceability, version sync, rollback API, publish webhook) are well-defined enough to become actionable backlog items. Creating them now ensures they don't get lost.

options.label: Leave as recommendations only
options.rationale: Let the initiative owner decide which to pursue. Avoids creating items that may not align with current priorities.

options.label: Create backlog items for all gaps (P1-P4)
options.rationale: Be comprehensive — even P3/P4 items like auto-deploy and documentation fixes are worth tracking.

items.topic: Where should the finalized system contract live long-term?
items.context: Currently the system contract lives in this research item's plan.md. Once finalized, downstream implementation items need to reference it. It could stay here (with a stable path), be promoted to a shared docs location, or be split per-scenario.

options.label: Keep in this research item (reference by backlog path)
options.rationale: Simplest approach. The swarm-manager backlog system provides a stable path. Other items can reference it via `swarm-manager backlog file-get --kind research --name desktop-release-control-plane-audit --path plan.md`.

options.label: Promote to docs/deployment/desktop-release-contract.md
options.rationale: Makes it discoverable outside the backlog system. Could be versioned with the codebase. But adds a maintenance burden to keep it in sync.

options.label: Split per-scenario into each scenario's docs/
options.rationale: Each scenario gets only its own contract section. Most distributed but hardest to maintain as a coherent whole.

plan_updates: Major update: (1) Added exhaustive action inventory for all 5 systems with endpoint counts, paths, and purposes. (2) Added 5 interface boundary contracts (deployment-manager, scenario-to-desktop, LPBS, scenario-to-cloud, prompt-manager skills) documenting owns/exposes/consumes/assumes. (3) Added prioritized gap recommendations table (P1-P4) with effort estimates. (4) Updated testing plan with completed validation items. (5) Checked off 7 of 8 Definition of Done items. (6) Discovered auth boundary detail: LPBS set-current is admin-only while apply accepts service auth.
